supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:52 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-DREYES-01 as paul.becker with the command line `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\FILE-COP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1`. The Sysmon and Windows process-creation records agree on the command and account.
The PowerShell process used logon ID 0xadda457, matching a network logon for paul.becker to WS-DREYES-01 from 10.52.10.23 recorded shortly beforehand.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update, and Windows Update traffic totaling about 38.8 MB was recorded at approximately the same time. This is consistent with the documented workstation-patching procedure and business-hours patch schedule.
The only PowerShell process creation shown in the reviewed interval is at 13:44:52 UTC, several minutes after the reported approximate time of 13:40 UTC.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process-creation records show PowerShell execution and its command line, but do not establish whether a window was visible to Dan Reyes. (T114-00312, T114-00313)
The logged PowerShell start is at 13:44:52 UTC, not exactly 13:40 UTC, so the records do not conclusively tie that process to the precise moment Dan noticed a window. (T114-00312, T114-00313)
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish exactly what Dan saw or the precise time he saw it. (T114-00312, T114-00313)
The records show the patch script path but not the script contents or its integrity. (T114-00312, T114-00313)
unrelated_findings: Separate review: Dan Reyes had network logons to WS-DREYES-01 from WS-KNGUYEN-01 at 13:40 and WS-SALI-01 at 13:45. These records are distinct from the PowerShell process and do not determine this alert. (T114-00140, T114-00142, T114-00333, T114-00334)

Separate review: Kerberos records show paul.becker authentication activity from WS-DREYES-01 (10.52.10.21) to WS-PBECKER-01 at 13:32. This is outside the alerted PowerShell activity; validate its context separately. (T114-00036, T114-00037, T114-00039)

Separate policy review: process-exit records show Dropbox, Cisco AnyConnect, and Google Drive File Stream processes on WS-DREYES-01. These are not part of the alerted PowerShell activity. (T114-00430, T114-00431, T114-00432, T114-00433, T114-00434, T114-00435)
